title: Compress retaining legs before installing a cage fastener
instruction: Fit the blue spring cage fastener into the square opening in the rack coupon. Compress both spring legs before passing the hooks through the opening. Release the legs behind the coupon so both hooks retain it. Keep the coupon within 5 mm and 5 degrees of its starting pose. Release both grippers when the fastener is seated. All equipment is unpowered.
context: Spring retained panel hardware requires compression during installation followed by release behind a thin plate. A robot must coordinate this change of contact state while supporting a loose workpiece. This scaled prototype tests that operation with two guided retaining legs. It does not require electrical contact or a mating socket.
setup: Use the official bimanual YAM station with the table at z 0.7475 m. x points away from the robots. y points left. z points up. Both objects are rigid plastic prototypes. Use ballast to match the stated masses. The grey rack coupon is loose and has total mass 240 g. Its root is x 280 mm and y negative 70 mm and z 40 mm above the table with zero yaw. Its square plate is 80 mm wide and 4 mm thick with a 34 mm square opening. Its top is 60 mm above the table. Four feet support the plate. An extended tab reaches toward positive y for the left gripper. Its overall bounds are 80 mm by 220 mm by 80 mm. The initial bounding box centre is x 280 mm and y 0 mm and z 40 mm above the table. The blue fastener root starts at x 170 mm and y negative 200 mm and z 6 mm above the table with zero yaw. Its overall bounds are 52 mm by 42 mm by 48 mm. The initial bounding box centre is 24 mm above the table. The root mass is 40 g and each sliding leg is 6 g. Each leg moves inward through an 8 mm guided stroke. Each spring rate is 80 N per metre with a 2 N force limit and linear damping of 1.2 N seconds per metre. The 52 mm upper flange and the lower hooks have a 6 mm vertical gap for the 4 mm plate. Both sliders start at their outer stops. scene_inventory.json gives every local solid and joint anchor. No other task objects are used.
scoring: The episode scores zero if the coupon bounding box centre moves more than 5 mm from its initial position or its rotation exceeds 5 degrees. Dropping the fastener more than 8 mm below the tabletop also scores zero. Otherwise score 0.25 when the fastener centre is within 30 mm horizontally of the target and its bottom is more than 20 mm above the table. Score 0.5 when its centre is within 6 mm on every axis of the target with tilt and yaw error below 5 degrees. A half turn about z is equivalent. Score 0.75 when the centre is within 3 mm on every axis with the same orientation limits and both sliders are within 1.5 mm of their outer stops and both sliders have previously been compressed more than 5 mm at the same observed time and each leg remains compressed by at least 4 mm while its hook top passes through the coupon plane and the centre varies by less than 1 mm over 20 consecutive samples. Score 1.0 for that installation with both measured grippers open beyond 35 mm of finger travel. The target centre is x 280 mm and y negative 70 mm and z 74 mm above the table. Full success must hold for one second. Conditions are checked at 20 Hz. All other outcomes score zero. The scorer returns the highest currently satisfied partial credit. The crossing monitor measures hook top centres in the actual coupon frame. The monitored band is 16 mm to 22 mm above the coupon root. Both hook tops must pass from above 22 mm to 16 mm or below within 25 mm horizontally of the opening. Starting a new approach clears crossing credit.
run_limit: 2400 control steps at 20 Hz. This is 120 seconds of control time.
reset_notes: Restore both root poses from scene_inventory.json. Place the fastener upright. Return both passive sliders to their outer stops. Restore the loose coupon without fastening it to the table. Nothing is consumed. Use seed 0 and object_jitter=0 for the recorded layout. Run one epoch per process.
fidelity: Rigid cuboid contact geometry on the official bimanual YAM rig. Two force limited prismatic spring joints represent guided retaining legs. Slider guides are ideal joints. The flange and hooks have physical collision geometry. Compound contact offsets are 1 mm. Contact materials use simulator defaults. Parts do not deform or fracture. Spring hysteresis and wear are omitted. History checks run at 20 Hz.
